chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from some of our companions, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It makes no difference to me whether you entrust [the wealth] to a treacherous person or to one who wastes it.

key_terms.أُبَالِي: I care / It makes no difference to me
key_terms.خَائِنٌ: Treacherous person / One who betrays trust

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between entrusting wealth to a dishonest person versus a wasteful one according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights a pragmatic distinction in fiduciary management, prioritizing the preservation of capital over moral integrity in the trustee. This teaching reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *hifz al-mal* (preservation of wealth), where the risk of gradual depletion through wastage (*israf*) is often viewed as more detrimental to the owner's long-term stability than the quicker, albeit dishonest, loss via theft. It underscores the practical reality that a trustworthy but careless individual may erode wealth through negligence, whereas a thief typically takes a fixed portion, leaving the remainder intact.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from sone of our companions, from Amro Bin Abu Al Miqdam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It makes no difference whether you trust and untrustworthy one or waste it’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from abu al-Rabi‘ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘If one trusts one who drinks wine, about a trust after knowing that he drinks wine, he has no guarantee for it before Allah or any reward or replacement for his loss.’”
